body:
# Issue #1: Fix Mocking for WordPress Functions and Re-enable Admin Tests

**Description:**

During CI setup and debugging, several WordPress core functions (`wp_create_nonce`, `wp_localize_script`) caused fatal errors in PHPUnit tests because they were not properly mocked using `WP_Mock`.

To allow the CI pipeline (PHPUnit & PHPCS) to pass, the following temporary measures were taken:

1.  **Commented out `wp_create_nonce` call:** The call to `wp_create_nonce()` within the [enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) method in `includes/Admin/class-admin.php` was commented out.
2.  **Commented out `wp_localize_script` call:** The call to `wp_localize_script()` within the [enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) method in `includes/Admin/class-admin.php` was commented out.
3.  **Commented out [test_enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) test:** The entire test method [test_enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) in [tests/test-admin.php](cci:7://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:0:0-0:0) was commented out as it directly triggered the errors related to the unmocked functions.

**Task:**

*   Implement proper mocking for `wp_create_nonce()` and `wp_localize_script()` within the [test_enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) method using `WP_Mock::userFunction()`. Ensure the mock expectations match the actual function calls in `includes/Admin/class-admin.php`.
*   Uncomment the calls to `wp_create_nonce()` and `wp_localize_script()` in `includes/Admin/class-admin.php`.
*   Uncomment the [test_enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) test method in [tests/test-admin.php](cci:7://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:0:0-0:0).
*   Verify that all PHPUnit tests pass after these changes.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*   All mocks for WordPress functions are correctly implemented in [tests/test-admin.php](cci:7://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:0:0-0:0).
*   All previously commented-out code related to these functions is restored.
*   The [test_enqueue_admin_assets](cci:1://file:///Users/marcusquinn/Git/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/tests/test-admin.php:67:4-152:5) test passes successfully.
*   The CI pipeline passes for all PHP versions (7.4, 8.0) and PHPCS checks.

title: fix: namespace mismatch, XSS in showMessage/showNotice, PHP 7.0 matrix compat, Plugin::init() not called
body:
## Summary

CodeRabbit review of PR #18 identified several actionable issues that should be fixed before merging. All CI checks are green but these are functional/security bugs not caught by the test suite.

## Issues Found

### Critical — Namespace mismatch breaks Multisite autoloading

`includes/Multisite/class-multisite.php` declares namespace `WP_Plugin_Starter_Template_For_AI_Coding\Multisite` but the autoloader registered via `spl_autoload_register` expects `WPALLSTARS\PluginStarterTemplate\`. The autoloader returns early without loading the file — the Multisite class cannot be instantiated via autoloading.

**Fix:** Update namespace in `includes/Multisite/class-multisite.php` to `WPALLSTARS\PluginStarterTemplate\Multisite`.

### Major — PHP 7.0 matrix + antecedent/patchwork incompatibility

`antecedent/patchwork@2.2.1` in `require-dev` requires PHP >=7.1.0. PHP 7.0 is still in the test matrix. The PHP 7.0 job will fail at `composer install`.

**Fix:** Either restore the PHP 7.0-specific `composer require --dev phpunit/phpunit:"^6.5"` branch in `tests.yml`, or remove `7.0` from the matrix.

### Security — XSS in showNotice / showMessage (admin JS)

- `admin/js/admin-scripts.js` `showNotice()` injects `message` directly into HTML via string interpolation — allows admin-side XSS
- `admin/js/update-source-selector.js` `showMessage()` uses `$message.html(message)` with server-provided content

**Fix:** Use `.text(message)` or DOM APIs instead of `.html()` / string interpolation.

### Bug — Plugin::init() never called from bootstrap

`wp-plugin-starter-template.php` line 38 constructs `Plugin` but never calls `init()`. Any initialisation logic added to `init()` will silently not run.

**Fix:**
```php
$plugin = new WPALLSTARS\PluginStarterTemplate\Plugin( __FILE__, '0.1.7' );
$plugin->init();
```

### Minor — PSR-4 filename mismatch

`includes/class-core.php` and `includes/class-plugin.php` use WordPress naming convention but the namespace expects PSR-4 (`Core.php`, `Plugin.php`). Either rename files or add explicit `require_once` in bootstrap.

### Minor — Tab indentation in new PHP files

`includes/class-core.php`, `includes/class-plugin.php`, `admin/templates/modal.php`, `includes/Admin/class-admin.php` use tabs; project standard is 4 spaces.

## Source

CodeRabbit review on PR #18: https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/pull/18

title: bug: install-wp-tests.sh fails with 'tags/6.9.4 not found' on PHP 7.4 WP latest matrix
body:
## Description

`bin/install-wp-tests.sh` fails on the `PHP 7.4 - WP latest - Single Site` CI matrix with:

```
fatal: Remote branch tags/6.9.4 not found in upstream origin
Error: Failed to clone wordpress-develop at branch/tag tags/6.9.4
```

## Evidence

- PR #54 (branch `quality-debt/wp-plugin-29`) CI run 23167807989 failed on this step
- The script attempts to clone `wordpress-develop` at `tags/6.9.4` but this tag does not exist in the upstream repo
- Other matrix entries (PHP 7.4 unit tests, PHP 8.0) pass — only the WP latest integration test is affected

## Root Cause

The `install-wp-tests.sh` script hardcodes or derives a WordPress version tag (`6.9.4`) that does not exist in the `wordpress-develop` repository. The latest stable WordPress is 6.7.x as of this filing. The script likely needs to use a valid tag or fall back to `trunk`.

## Fix

Update `bin/install-wp-tests.sh` to use a valid WordPress develop tag (e.g., `6.7`) or use `trunk` when the derived tag is not found. Add a fallback mechanism to prevent hard failures on version mismatches.

title: bug: CI intermittently fails with Packagist DNS timeout (curl error 28)
body:
## Description

Multiple CI runs fail intermittently with Packagist DNS resolution timeouts:

```
curl error 28 while downloading https://repo.packagist.org/packages.json: Resolving timed out after 10001 milliseconds
The following exception probably indicates you have misconfigured DNS resolver(s)
```

## Evidence

- PR #51 (branch `quality-debt/wp-plugin-45`) run 23163744921 — PHPStan job failed
- PR #49 (branch `quality-debt/wp-plugin-41`) run 23163634319 — PHP CodeSniffer job failed (rerun succeeded)
- Both failures are in the `composer require --dev` step, not in the actual code

## Impact

Transient failures block otherwise-passing PRs from merging. The code changes are correct but CI is unreliable.

## Fix Options

1. Add retry logic to composer install steps in CI workflows
2. Pre-install composer dependencies in a cached step before the analysis jobs
3. Use `--prefer-dist` and increase timeout in composer config
4. Add `COMPOSER_DISABLE_NETWORK=1` fallback with pre-cached vendor directory

title: fix: pin GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs to resolve SonarCloud security gate
body:
## Problem

SonarCloud quality gate is failing with ERROR status due to unreviewed security hotspots (S7637: Use full commit SHA hash for dependencies).

**Failing conditions:**
- `new_security_rating`: actual=3, required GT 1 — new vulnerabilities introduced
- `new_security_hotspots_reviewed`: actual=0.0, required LT 100 — 14 unreviewed hotspots

## Root Cause

Multiple GitHub Actions workflows use floating version tags (`@v2`, `@v3`, `@v4`) instead of pinned full commit SHAs. This is a supply chain security risk (SonarCloud S7637).

## Affected Files

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` — `shivammathur/setup-php@v2` (3x), `codacy/codacy-analysis-cli-action@v4`, `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3`
- `.github/workflows/phpunit.yml` — `shivammathur/setup-php@v2`
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml` — `actions/checkout@v4` (2x), `shivammathur/setup-php@v2` (2x)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — `actions/checkout@v3`, `shivammathur/setup-php@v2`, `softprops/action-gh-release@v1`
- `.github/workflows/sync-wiki.yml` — `actions/checkout@v3`
- `.github/workflows/playground-tests.yml` — `actions/setup-node@v4` (3x), `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (2x), `swissspidy/wp-performance-action@v2.0.3`
- `.github/workflows/wordpress-tests.yml` — `actions/setup-node@v4` (2x), `actions/upload-artifact@v4`
- `.github/workflows/playground-tests-fix.yml` — `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`

## Fix

Pin each action to its full commit SHA. Use `gh api` to resolve the SHA for each action version, then update the workflow files with the format:
```
uses: owner/action@<full-sha> # vX.Y.Z
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All floating `@vX` tags replaced with full commit SHAs + version comment
- [ ] SonarCloud security hotspots resolved (gate passes)
- [ ] CI passes on the PR

title: fix: resolve SonarCloud security gate — review S7636 hotspots in GitHub Actions workflows
body:
## Problem

SonarCloud quality gate is **ERROR** due to 3 unreviewed security hotspots (rule `githubactions:S7636` — secrets expanded in run blocks). The gate condition `new_security_hotspots_reviewed` is 0.0% (required: 100%).

This blocks the SonarCloud badge from showing green.

## Affected files

| File | Line | Finding |
|------|------|---------|
| `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` | 147 | Avoid expanding secrets in a run block |
| `.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml` | 43 | Avoid expanding secrets in a run block |
| `.github/workflows/sync-wiki.yml` | 53 | Avoid expanding secrets in a run block |

## Fix options

**Option A — Mark as Safe in SonarCloud UI** (no code change needed)
If the secret expansion is intentional and safe (e.g., passing a token to a CLI tool that requires it as an argument), mark each hotspot as "Safe" in the SonarCloud project dashboard. This resolves the gate without code changes.

**Option B — Refactor to use `env:` block**
Move secret references from inline `${{ secrets.X }}` in `run:` steps to the step's `env:` block:

```yaml
# Before (triggers S7636)
- run: some-tool --token ${{ secrets.MY_TOKEN }}

# After (safe)
- run: some-tool --token "$MY_TOKEN"
  env:
    MY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MY_TOKEN }}
```

The `env:` approach prevents the secret from appearing in the workflow's expanded command string.

## Priority

High — this is the primary reason the SonarCloud gate shows ERROR. Fixing or acknowledging these 3 hotspots will restore the gate to OK.

## Source

Detected by daily quality sweep 2026-03-18. See issue #92 for full sweep details.

title: fix: resolve 2 remaining SonarCloud VULNERABILITY issues blocking quality gate
body:
## Summary

PR #138 resolved 130 SonarCloud violations but 2 VULNERABILITY issues remain that block the quality gate (`new_security_rating: 3`).

Identified by CodeRabbit analysis on issue #92.

## Vulnerabilities to Fix

### VULNERABILITY #1 — `includes/Admin/class-admin.php` line 56

`$_GET['page']` is passed through `wp_unslash()` only. SonarCloud taint analysis requires an explicit sanitizer. `wp_unslash` removes slashes but is **not** a sanitizer.

```diff
-            // phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.ValidatedSanitizedInput.InputNotSanitized -- We're sanitizing with wp_unslash and validating later
-            $page = isset( $_GET['page'] ) ? \wp_unslash( $_GET['page'] ) : '';
+            // phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.NonceVerification.Recommended -- Page slug only used for conditional asset loading; no state change occurs
+            $page = isset( $_GET['page'] ) ? sanitize_text_field( \wp_unslash( $_GET['page'] ) ) : '';
```

### VULNERABILITY #2 — `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` line 113

The commented-out sonarcloud job block contains `${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}` expanded inside a `run:` shell context. SonarCloud Automatic Analysis parses YAML including comments and classifies this as a VULNERABILITY. The block is fully redundant — `sonarcloud.yml` handles all SonarCloud analysis.

Fix: remove the entire commented-out sonarcloud job block (lines ~84–134).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `sanitize_text_field()` wraps `wp_unslash()` in `includes/Admin/class-admin.php`
- [ ] Commented-out sonarcloud block removed from `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`
- [ ] PHPCS passes with zero violations
- [ ] ShellCheck passes with zero violations
- [ ] SonarCloud quality gate returns to PASSED

Closes #92 (pending next quality sweep confirmation)

title: Resolve 21 Dependabot security alerts in dev dependencies
body:
## What

Resolve 21 open Dependabot vulnerability alerts (2 critical, 8 high, 8 medium, 3 low). All alerts are in dev-only dependencies (build/test tooling) — plugin runtime is unaffected.

Snapshot at filing time:

- Critical: `simple-git` <3.32.3 (RCE), `form-data` <4.0.4 (unsafe boundary RNG)
- High: `simple-git` <3.32.0, `lodash` <4.18.0, `fast-xml-parser` <5.5.6, `minimatch` <3.1.3, `fast-xml-parser` <5.3.6, `fast-xml-parser` <5.3.4, `phpunit/phpunit` <9.6.33, `jws` <3.2.3
- Medium: `fast-xml-parser` (3 advisories), `lodash` <4.18.0, `picomatch` (2 advisories), `lodash` <4.17.23, `qs` <6.14.1, `js-yaml` <3.14.2
- Low: `fast-xml-parser` <5.3.8, `qs` <6.14.2, `tmp` <=0.2.3

## Why

- Critical/high RCE alerts on `simple-git`, `form-data`, `lodash`, `jws` are reachable in local dev and CI.
- This repo is a starter template — its dependency posture propagates to anyone who clones it.
- Repo-level `dependabot_security_updates` is currently **disabled** and `.github/dependabot.yml` does not exist, so Dependabot scans but never opens fix PRs. Without enabling these, every transitive vuln has to be hand-fixed forever.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: package.json` — add `overrides` block to force minimum-safe versions of stuck transitives. Targets:
    - `lodash@^4.18.0`
    - `qs@^6.14.2`
    - `tmp@^0.2.4`
    - `simple-git@^3.32.3`
    - `form-data@^4.0.4`
    - `fast-xml-parser@^5.7.0`
    - `minimatch@^3.1.3`
    - `jws@^3.2.3`
    - `js-yaml@^3.14.2`
    - `picomatch@^4.0.4`
- `EDIT: package-lock.json` — regenerate via `npm install`.
- `EDIT: composer.lock` — regenerate via `composer update phpunit/phpunit --with-all-dependencies` (current constraint `^9.5.0` already permits 9.6.33; no `composer.json` edit needed).
- `NEW: .github/dependabot.yml` — schedule weekly npm + composer + github-actions version updates with grouped minor/patch.
- One-shot API call (not committed; documented in PR body): `gh api -X PUT /repos/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/automated-security-fixes` to enable security updates at the repo level.

### Reference pattern

- npm `overrides` syntax: <https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/configuring-npm/package-json#overrides>.
- Existing `.github/workflows/*.yml` show the project's CI conventions (full SHA pinning per PR #90).
- Dependabot config schema: <https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference>.

### Verification

- `npm install && npm audit --audit-level=low` → 0 vulnerabilities.
- `composer install && composer audit` → 0 advisories.
- `npm run lint:js` → no errors (tooling still wired correctly).
- After merge, all 21 alert numbers should transition to `auto_dismissed` or `fixed` on Dependabot's next scan.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities at all severity levels.
- [ ] `composer audit` reports 0 advisories.
- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` committed with weekly npm + composer + github-actions schedules.
- [ ] Repo-level `dependabot_security_updates` is enabled (verified via `gh api /repos/.../automated-security-fixes`).
- [ ] CI green on the PR (lint, phpunit, playground tests).
- [ ] Plugin runtime behaviour unchanged — only dev dep manifests touched.

## Context

- Session origin: user shared the Dependabot alerts URL with no other instruction; agent triaged.
- Discovery: 21 open alerts, all in dev-deps; no open Dependabot PRs because `dependabot_security_updates` is disabled and `dependabot.yml` is absent.
- Memory recall returned no prior lessons on this repo's Dependabot triage.

title: consolidated: bump WordPress Playground CLI and fast-xml-parser
body:
_Supersedes #165 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Update the JavaScript dependency set that powers WordPress Playground tooling:

* Bump `@wp-playground/cli` from the current manifest range `^3.0.22` to `^3.1.21`.
* Keep `@wp-playground/client` aligned at `^3.1.21`.
* Ensure the lockfile resolves `@wp-playground/cli` to `3.1.21` and keeps its workspace packages aligned at `3.1.21`.
* Ensure `fast-xml-parser` resolves to `5.7.2`; align the root override to `^5.7.2` so the manifest reflects the resolved security/reliability target instead of only relying on the lockfile.

## Why

The original dependency PR became dirty against the default branch and lacked an `origin:*` label, so the pulse surfaced it for consolidation rather than continuing to re-evaluate a conflicted branch. A fresh implementation issue should preserve the dependency intent while avoiding the stale PR state.

The dependency updates need to be handled together because `@wp-playground/cli` brings the updated Playground package graph and depends on `fast-xml-parser`; the parser update includes fixes for long tag expressions, `attributesGroupName` with `preserveOrder`, numerical external entity backward compatibility, entity-handling changes via `@nodable/entities`, and CDATA/comment sanitization in `fast-xml-builder`.

## How

Files to modify:

* EDIT: `package.json:63-82` — update `devDependencies.@wp-playground/cli` from `^3.0.22` to `^3.1.21`; keep `@wp-playground/client` at `^3.1.21`; update `overrides.fast-xml-parser` from `^5.7.0` to `^5.7.2`.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:11-15` — ensure the root package `devDependencies` reflect the manifest range for `@wp-playground/cli`.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:2363-2410` — ensure `node_modules/@wp-playground/cli` remains resolved to `3.1.21` with its `3.1.21` Playground dependencies.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:4645-4665` — ensure `node_modules/fast-xml-parser` remains resolved to `5.7.2` with `@nodable/entities`, `fast-xml-builder`, `path-expression-matcher`, and `strnum` dependencies.

Reference pattern:

* Model the lockfile update on the existing resolved entries already present in `package-lock.json` for `@wp-playground/cli` `3.1.21` and `fast-xml-parser` `5.7.2`.
* Do not resurrect or rebase the stale Dependabot branch from #165; implement from the current default branch so the PR has a focused dependency diff.

Verification:

* `npm install --package-lock-only`
* `npm run lint:js`
* `npm run lint:css`
* `npm run lint:php:simple`

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] `package.json` declares `@wp-playground/cli` as `^3.1.21`.
* [ ] `package.json` keeps `@wp-playground/client` at `^3.1.21`.
* [ ] `package.json` declares the `fast-xml-parser` override as `^5.7.2`.
* [ ] `package-lock.json` resolves `node_modules/@wp-playground/cli` to `3.1.21`.
* [ ] `package-lock.json` resolves `node_modules/fast-xml-parser` to `5.7.2`.
* [ ] The dependency update is implemented in a fresh focused PR rather than by rebasing the conflicted #165 branch.
* [ ] The listed npm and lint verification commands pass, or any environment-specific failure is documented with command output.

## Context & Decisions

* Original problem statement from @marcusquinn via Dependabot: bump `fast-xml-parser` from `5.3.0` to `5.7.2` and update ancestor dependency `@wp-playground/cli` from `3.0.22` to `3.1.21`; these dependencies should be updated together.
* Per @marcusquinn's first pulse escalation comment: #165 was dirty and not auto-resolvable, so it required maintainer action rather than automatic merge.
* Per @marcusquinn's second pulse rebase nudge: #165 also lacked an `origin:*` label, which caused the pulse to treat it as a label-agnostic stuck PR and surface a one-shot rebase nudge.
* Final approach: supersede the conflicted dependency PR with this consolidated worker-ready issue, then implement from current `origin/main` with explicit `origin:worker` provenance.
* Rejected/superseded approach: do not continue discussion or implementation on #165; it is superseded by this issue.

title: consolidated: bump picomatch for security fixes
body:
_Supersedes #163 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Update the JavaScript dependency graph so `picomatch` resolves to the security-fixed release line surfaced by Dependabot:

* `picomatch` `4.0.3` → `4.0.4` for the primary lockfile entry.
* Transitive `picomatch` `2.3.1` → `2.3.2` where the dependency graph still resolves the v2 line.
* Keep the associated dependency updates together because the original Dependabot body states these dependencies need to be updated as a set.

## Why

`picomatch` `4.0.4` is a security release fixing security-relevant issues disclosed as:

* `GHSA-c2c7-rcm5-vvqj` / `CVE-2026-33671`.
* `GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p` / `CVE-2026-33672`.

The previous Dependabot PR became dirty against the default branch and lacked an origin label, so the pulse could not safely auto-merge it. This consolidated issue replaces that conflicted PR with a worker-ready spec that can be implemented from a clean branch.

## How

* EDIT: `package.json:75-86` — keep or add an `overrides.picomatch` entry resolving to `^4.0.4`, following the existing overrides pattern in that block.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:6304` — refresh the lockfile so dependencies requiring the v2 line resolve to the patched compatible release (`^2.3.2`) if npm produces a separate v2 entry.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:6521` — refresh the lockfile so dependencies requiring the v4 line allow the patched release.
* EDIT: `package-lock.json:7031-7039` — ensure the concrete `node_modules/picomatch` package entry resolves to `4.0.4` with the matching npm registry tarball and integrity.
* Run the dependency update from the existing manifests rather than editing lockfile internals by hand when possible: `npm install --package-lock-only` after adjusting any necessary override.
* Do not re-open or depend on the superseded Dependabot branch; implement from the current default branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] `package.json` contains an override or dependency constraint ensuring `picomatch` resolves to `^4.0.4` for the active v4 line.
* [ ] `package-lock.json` contains no vulnerable `picomatch` concrete package entry for `4.0.3` or earlier on the v4 line.
* [ ] If a v2 `picomatch` concrete package entry exists, it resolves to `2.3.2` or newer on the v2 line.
* [ ] `npm install --package-lock-only` completes without lockfile conflicts.
* [ ] `npm audit --omit=dev` or the repository's chosen audit command does not report the cited `picomatch` advisories as unresolved for production dependencies.
* [ ] The implementation PR uses `Resolves #<this issue>` and records the dependency-update verification in the PR body.

## Context & Decisions

* Original Dependabot body: reported a combined dependency update for `picomatch`, with the v4 line moving from `4.0.3` to `4.0.4` and the v2 line moving from `2.3.1` to `2.3.2`; it also included the upstream release note that `4.0.4` fixes `CVE-2026-33671` and `CVE-2026-33672`.
* Per @marcusquinn at 2026-04-29T09:28:13Z: the original PR was `DIRTY` with merge conflicts and did not meet auto-rebase or auto-close criteria, so maintainer review was needed rather than automatic merge.
* Per @marcusquinn at 2026-04-30T19:45:30Z: the PR also lacked both `origin:interactive` and `origin:worker`, causing it to fall into the label-agnostic stuck state. The correct replacement is a fresh worker-origin issue rather than continuing with the unlabeled conflicted PR.
* Rejected/superseded path: manually rebasing the old Dependabot branch is no longer the preferred path for autonomous work because this issue is the consolidated spec and the prior thread is superseded.
* Final approach: implement the dependency update from a clean branch against current default, using `package.json` and `package-lock.json` as the source of truth, and verify with npm lockfile/audit commands.

title: fix: sync-core.sh default starter folder name gets renamed in synced plugins
body:
## What

`scripts/sync-core.sh` is a core file. When it is copied into a plugin, the name substitution also rewrites its default starter folder name: in SEO Pro Stack it reads

```

```

## Where

- `scripts/sync-core.sh` (the `STARTER_REPO_DIR` constant and the `--from DIR` usage line), in this starter repository.
- The substitution itself is in the same script (and `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` if names are listed there): it replaces the starter's slug everywhere in core files.

### Files Scope

## Do

Keep the starter's own repository name out of the substitution, for example by building it from parts (`STARTER_REPO_DIR="wp-plugin-starter-template""-for-ai-coding"`), or by marking the line so the substitution skips it. Use whichever pattern the script already has for names that must stay the starter's. Then run `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` from a plugin made from the starter, for example `wpallstars/seoprostack`.

title: fix: guard settings option callbacks so one failing list cannot stop every page
body:
## Problem

`{Prefix}_Settings::options_for()` (`includes/class-{prefix}-settings.php`) calls each select/multi field's `options` callback with no guard. `maybe_migrate()` → `sanitize_all()` → `sanitize_value()` calls it on the first request after any `DB_VERSION` bump, front end included. If one callback throws, every page on that site shows a critical error. The upgrade never finishes, so this repeats on every request.

Seen in SEO Pro Stack 0.11.3 (wpallstars/seoprostack#273): `SEOProStack_Agency_Orders::form_options()` queried Fluent Forms' `Form` model on network sites where Fluent Forms was network-active but its tables were never created. That release fixed the plugin's own callbacks; this issue is the core guard, so no other plugin made from the starter can hit the same thing.

## Change

In `includes/class-{prefix}-settings.php`, `options_for()`: wrap the `call_user_func($field['options'])` call in `try { … } catch (\Throwable $e) { return array(); }`. Keep PHP 7.4 syntax. With an empty list, open fields (`'open' => true`) keep stored values. Closed fields fall back to their default, which is the right result when their source is broken.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.
- A temporary callback that throws (`'options' => function () { throw new \RuntimeException('x'); }`) on a throwaway site: the front page still loads and `{prefix}_db_version` advances.
- Then `scripts/sync-core.sh` in each plugin made from the starter (SEO Pro Stack first).

title: rename-plugin.sh: set the maker's details (description, author, links)
body:
## What

`scripts/rename-plugin.sh` gives a copy of the starter its own names, but not its maker's details. A plugin made by anyone else keeps the starter's `Author`, `Author URI` and `Description` headers, `readme.txt` `Contributors` and `Donate link`, and the settings screen's website and donate buttons (`header_links()` in the Setup class).

## Change

Add optional flags; each one left out keeps the starter's value:

- `--description` (one line, up to 150 characters): Description header, readme.txt short description, the line under README.md's title
- `--author`: Author header
- `--author-uri`: Author URI header and the `website` header link
- `--plugin-uri`: Plugin URI header (default stays the GitHub repository page)
- `--contributors`: readme.txt Contributors
- `--donate URL|none`: readme.txt Donate link and the `donate` header link; `none` removes both

Values are checked before anything changes (URLs must be http(s), no `*/` or new lines in header text, description at most 150 characters).

## Files

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`: flags, `set_identity()` and helpers (`set_field`, `set_line`, `set_link`, `replace_with_tmp`)
- `README.md`: Start a plugin step 2

## Verification

On a throwaway clone: rename with every flag (values containing `&`, `/`, `\` and quotes), then `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh`; a second clone with only some flags keeps the starter's other values; invalid values are refused before any change.

Stop SonarCloud and Codacy reporting rules that conflict with WordPress coding standards, so their dashboards show real findings.

## Noise to silence (about 300 of 478 findings)

SonarCloud (`wpallstars_wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`):

- `php:S100` (80): method names must be camelCase. WordPress requires snake_case (PHPCS enforces it).
- `php:S101` (9): class names `WPStarter_Admin_Manager`: WordPress class naming.
- `php:S116` (2): field naming, same reason.
- `php:S1142` (8): max 3 returns. Early-return guards are the project style.

title: bug: GitHub-only builds can be updated to an unrelated WordPress.org plugin with the same slug
body:
Parent: #281

## What

A GitHub-only plugin can be "updated" to an unrelated WordPress.org plugin that has the same slug. Found by the CodeRabbit full review on #281 (finding 1, high), confirmed in the code.

## Evidence

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:515-526` `on_wordpress_org()` returns true for any `response`/`no_update` entry whose `id` does not start with `ID_PREFIX` (`github.com/`). It never checks that the WordPress.org entry is this plugin.
- `:546-549` `add_updates()` then skips GitHub for that plugin (unless the `wpallstars_github_updater_early` filter is on), so core's WordPress.org offer stands.
- `STANDARDS.md` bans `Update URI` in the main file because WordPress.org rejects plugins that carry it, so GitHub-only builds have no protection from core's slug match against api.wordpress.org.

## Proposed fix

1. GitHub zip only: `scripts/build-release.sh` adds an `Update URI: https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}` header to the GitHub build's main file. The WordPress.org zip (built from `.distignore-wporg`) keeps the main file without it. With `Update URI` set to a non-wordpress.org host, core (5.8+) does not send the plugin to api.wordpress.org and fires `update_plugins_github.com`.
2. The updater: treat a plugin as "on WordPress.org" only when its installed header has no `Update URI` (or one on `w.org`/`wordpress.org`). Keep `on_wordpress_org()` for those builds.
3. `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: fail if the WordPress.org zip has `Update URI`, and fail if the GitHub zip lacks it.
4. Update `STANDARDS.md` (Updates from GitHub, Releases) and `RELEASING.md` to say which zip carries the header and why.

Check with Context7 / WordPress core (`wp-includes/update.php` `wp_update_plugins()`, the `update_plugins_{$hostname}` filter) before relying on it. Keep the minimum WordPress version in mind (`Requires at least` in the main file).

## Constraints

The updater class is shared: only the newest copy runs on a site with several wpallstars plugins. Do not rename the class or its public methods. Plugins without the new header (older releases) must keep working.

## Acceptance

- GitHub zip main file has `Update URI`; WordPress.org zip does not (`scripts/preflight-release.sh` enforces both).
- On a test site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`) with a plugin whose slug matches a WordPress.org plugin, only the GitHub release is offered.
- `scripts/lint.sh`, CI smoke tests and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` pass; Plugin Check on the WordPress.org zip has no new errors.

## Files Scope

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `scripts/build-release.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- `STANDARDS.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `changelog.txt`

title: bug: rename-plugin.sh writes unescaped names and URLs into PHP
body:
Parent: #281

## What

`scripts/rename-plugin.sh` accepts a plugin name or URL that breaks the generated PHP. Found by the CodeRabbit full review on #281 (finding 2, high), confirmed in the code.

## Evidence

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh:309` `need --name "$name" '^[^/\\]+$'` allows `'` and `"`.

- `set_link()` (`:122-137`) writes the URL inside `'…'` without escaping. The URL check allows `\` and `'`.

## Proposed fix

- Validate every value before any file changes: single line, no control characters; URLs `^https?://[^\s'"\\]+$`.
- Escape per context when writing: PHP single-quoted (`\` → `\\`, `'` → `\'`), plugin header / `readme.txt` (plain text, no newline), Markdown (as is).
- After renaming, run `php -l` on every changed `.php` file and stop with an error if one fails.

## Acceptance

- On a throwaway linked worktree: `scripts/rename-plugin.sh --slug owners-plugin --name "Owner's \"Best\" Plugin" --prefix Owners …` succeeds, `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs` passes, and the settings screen title shows the name exactly.

title: bug: updater caches failed requirement checks, picks loose assets, drops private download errors
body:
Parent: #281

## What

Four robustness gaps in the shared GitHub updater, from the CodeRabbit full review on #281 (findings 4, 5, 6, 11). Do this after the `Update URI` change is merged if both touch the same lines.

## Findings (`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`)

1. **Failed requirement fetch is cached as a good release** (`:393-398`, `:441-443`): if reading the released main file fails, `$body` is `''`, `requirements('')` returns empty `requires`/`requires_php`, and the release is cached for 12 hours with no compatibility data. Treat that failure as a retryable error (short cache, as for other request errors) instead of a release with unknown requirements.
2. **Authenticated asset choice is loose** (`pick_asset()`, `:455-468`): takes the first `.zip` whose name starts with the folder, so `my-plugin-tools.zip` or an older asset can win. The public path (`fetch_web()`, ~`:370`) asks for exactly `{folder}-{version}.zip`. Pass the version and require the exact name in both paths.
3. **Private download error is dropped** (`private_package()` and its fallback, ~`:715-750`): a `WP_Error` from `signed_address()` is discarded, the original API URL is kept and the fallback calls `signed_address()` again (two waits, original error lost). Keep the first result for this upgrade and return the error through the upgrader (`upgrader_pre_download` returning `WP_Error`). Keep the `upgrader_package_options` filter returning an array. Also check the signed address is `https://` on a GitHub download host before handing it to core.
4. **Docs** say the asset "whose name starts with" the slug: `README.md:74`, `RELEASING.md:26`, `STANDARDS.md:176`. Say `{slug}-{version}.zip` exactly.

## Constraints

Shared class: keep behaviour and public API, never follow redirects with the token, keep the token on `api.github.com` only.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes; CI smoke tests and Plugin Check pass.
- On a test site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`): blocking `raw.githubusercontent.com` (or the contents API) gives no update offer and a retry within the short error cache, not a 12-hour cached release.
- A release with `{slug}-tools.zip` listed before `{slug}-{version}.zip` installs the right zip with a token set.

## Files Scope

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `README.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `STANDARDS.md`, `changelog.txt`

title: bug: smoke-test, sync-core, plugin-check and preview-site can report success after a failure
body:
Parent: #281

## What

Four scripts can report success after a failure, plus one docs error. From the CodeRabbit full review on #281 (findings 7, 8, 9, 10, 12), each confirmed in the code.

## Findings

1. **`scripts/smoke-test.sh:144-148`**: on a connection failure curl's `-w '%{http_code}'` prints `000`, and `|| printf '000'` appends another, so `status` is `000000`. That is neither `= "000"` nor `-ge 500`, so the page is listed as fine. Also `$TMP_DIR/page` is not cleared first, so the critical-error grep can read the previous page. Fix: `rm -f` the page file, capture curl's exit code separately, fail on non-zero exit or status `000`/`>= 500`.
2. **`scripts/sync-core.sh:47-58, 113-137`**: `core_paths()` feeds the loop through `< <(…)`. If `git show "$ref:scripts/core-files.txt"` fails, the loop gets nothing and `--check` prints "All 0 core files match the starter." Fix: write the list to the temp file with a checked exit status, and die when it is empty.
3. **`scripts/plugin-check.sh:116-125, 179-182`**: `wp plugin check … || true` drops the exit code, and any `FILE: ` line counts as "it ran". A run that prints one file and then fails reports 0 errors. Fix: keep the exit code; treat non-zero with no parsed findings as "did not run". Plugin Check exits non-zero when there are errors, so parse first.
4. **`scripts/preview-site.sh:91`**: the lock is taken over if the owner is dead **or** the lock is older than `LOCK_STALE_MINUTES`, so a live run longer than 10 minutes loses it and two runs can `rsync --delete` the same site. Fix: take over only when the owner pid is gone (age only when there is no pid file).
5. **`DEVELOPMENT.md:186`** recommends "CodeQL (PHP and JavaScript)". CodeQL does not support PHP. Say CodeQL for JavaScript and Actions; PHP is covered by PHPStan, SonarCloud and Codacy.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh shell` passes (ShellCheck clean); CI smoke tests pass.
- smoke-test: with the web container stopped mid-run, `fetch` fails the run.
- sync-core: `--ref <a commit without scripts/core-files.txt>` exits non-zero with a clear message.
- preview-site: a second run waits while the first is alive, even after 10 minutes.

## Files Scope

- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/sync-core.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`, `scripts/preview-site.sh`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `changelog.txt`

title: bug: concurrent settings saves can overwrite each other
body:
Parent: #281

## What

Two saves at the same time can undo each other's change. From the CodeRabbit full review on #281 (finding 3, medium).

## Evidence

- `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:~217-225`: each save reads the whole options array, changes one key and writes the whole array with `update_option()`.
- `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js:~77-78, ~175-176`: the save queue only orders saves from one page. Two tabs or two admins saving different keys can both read the old array, and the later write drops the earlier change. Both may report success.

## Proposed fix

Keep one option (other code and `uninstall.php` rely on it). Make the write a compare-and-swap: read the stored value, apply the one change, write only if the stored value is unchanged since the read (re-read with the cache cleared, retry a few times). Or set a short lock with `add_option()` of a lock key (atomic in WordPress) around the read-modify-write. Pick the simpler one and say why in the PR.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes; CI smoke tests pass.
- Two concurrent `admin-ajax.php` saves of different keys (for example two `curl` calls in parallel against `scripts/preview-site.sh`'s site with a valid nonce and cookie) both persist.
- Single saves behave as before (same response, same verification message).

title: quality: remaining SonarCloud findings after CI analysis (a11y, regex, complexity)
body:
## What

SonarCloud now runs from CI with `sonar-project.properties` (#310), and the four WordPress-conflict rules are gone. 32 open findings remain on `main` at 07ba9be (`https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=wpallstars_wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding&resolved=false`). Fix the real ones, and resolve the intended ones in a visible, reasoned way. Behaviour, HTML structure, hooks, option keys and `wps-*` classes stay unchanged unless a finding is a real defect.

## Findings and expected outcome

**Likely defects (fix):**
- `php:S5869` ×2 `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php:161`: duplicate characters in a regex character class. Remove the duplicates; check the Read Me tab renders the same.
- `Web:S6807` ×2 `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:153` and `:548`: `role="switch"` without `aria-checked`. If the element is a native `<input type="checkbox">`, drop the redundant role or confirm the native `checked` state is exposed; otherwise add `aria-checked` kept in sync by `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`.
- `Web:S6819` `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:330` (`role="group"`) and `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:58` (`role="status"`): use the native element (`<fieldset>`/`<output>`) where it does not change layout, or keep the role with a `// NOSONAR` reason if the live-region behaviour depends on it.
- `php:S1488` `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php:392`: return the expression directly.
- `php:S1192` `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:181-182`: the admin CSS/JS paths repeated three times become class constants.

**Complexity (refactor into private helpers, output identical):**
- `php:S3776` `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php:39` (43), `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php:325` (32), `scripts/replaced-plugins.php:121` (22) and `:289` (17), `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:259` (19). Pattern: #285/#286 (control-specific private methods from a map).

**Intended (resolve with a reason, do not refactor):**
- `php:S1172` ×16 in `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php` (render_* methods, lines 359-562) and `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php` (sanitize_* methods, lines 446-569): renderers/sanitizers are chosen from a map and share one signature by design (#285, #286). Add one targeted ignore in `sonar-project.properties` scoped to those two files (`sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria` entry with ruleKey `php:S1172` and the exact resourceKeys), with a comment naming the dispatch map.
- `php:S1448` `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:20` (40 methods) and `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:48` (35 methods): the settings store is the public static API features call, and the updater is a shared single-file class every wpallstars plugin carries. Splitting either changes core-file layout for every plugin. Resolve as "Accepted" in SonarCloud with that reason, or a scoped ignore in `sonar-project.properties` with a comment; do not split.

## Files

`admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`, `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`, `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`, `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`, `scripts/replaced-plugins.php`, `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js` (only if `aria-checked` needs syncing), `sonar-project.properties`, `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, phpcs, phpstan, js, shell) passes.
- Settings screen HTML before/after compared for the refactors, as in #285 (identical apart from intended a11y changes); Read Me tab renders `README.md` identically.

title: feat: scheduled check that plugins made from the starter keep its core files
body:
## What

Plugins made from the starter fall behind when the starter's core files change: nothing tells them. Add a scheduled check that every plugin carries (a core file), which opens or updates one issue in the plugin when its core files differ from the starter's `main`, and closes it when they match again.

## How

- New core workflow `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml` (`.github/` is already in `scripts/core-files.txt`, so `scripts/sync-core.sh` delivers it; `.distignore` already keeps `.github` out of the zips).
  - Weekly schedule and `workflow_dispatch`; `permissions: contents: read, issues: write`.
  - Check out the plugin and the starter's `main` side by side; run the **starter's** `scripts/sync-core.sh --check --from <starter>` from the plugin (newest script; exit 0 match, 1 differ, 2 error → job fails).
  - Build the starter's `owner/repo` from split strings (as `STARTER_REPO_DIR` in `scripts/sync-core.sh`), because `plugin_map` rewrites the starter's repository and slug in every core file. Repository variable `STARTER_REPO` overrides it.
  - Skip in the starter itself.
  - One open issue, label `starter-sync`: create or update it with the starter commit, the differing/missing files, and worker-ready steps (`scripts/sync-core.sh`, review `git diff`, lint, smoke test; a change the plugin made to a core file goes into the starter first). Close it with a comment when all files match.
- Docs: `STANDARDS.md` → Structure (the check and what to do with its issue), `DEVELOPMENT.md` (setup: nothing for public starters; manual run; override variable), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (actionlint, shellcheck through it) passes.
- The workflow skips in the starter (manual run here).
- In a plugin made from the starter: a run with differing files opens one `starter-sync` issue; a second run updates it, not a new one; after `scripts/sync-core.sh` and a merge, a run closes it.
- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` on a throwaway clone keeps the starter's repository name in the workflow.

For #281

title: feat: scripts/update-test.sh checks a release updates from the previous one
body:
## What

Add a core script, `scripts/update-test.sh`, for `RELEASING.md` step 4: "on a site with the previous version, **Check again** on the Updates screen shows the update and that it installs". Today that step is done by hand. For releases 1.0.5, 1.0.6 and 1.0.7 it was checked with a throwaway script outside the repository, which every plugin made from the starter would have to rewrite. Make it a core file so every plugin gets it through `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## How

1. New file `scripts/update-test.sh`, listed in `scripts/core-files.txt` next to `scripts/smoke-test.sh`. Like the other scripts, take the plugin's names from its main file with `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` (`plugin_identity`, `plugin_header_field` for `GitHub Plugin URI`) and use no plugin's names in the code.
2. Start a throwaway WordPress in Docker the same way `scripts/smoke-test.sh` does (lines 79–105: network, volume, `mariadb:10.6` or `plugin_env DB_IMAGE`, `wordpress:cli-php$PHP_VERSION`, `wordpress:php$PHP_VERSION-apache` on `127.0.0.1::80`, `WP_DEBUG_LOG` on, `DISABLE_WP_CRON`). Remove everything on exit with a `trap`. If sharing the site set-up with `smoke-test.sh` through a new `scripts/lib/` file is simple, do it, but leave `smoke-test.sh`'s behaviour unchanged.
3. Options: `--from VERSION` (default: the release before the newest), `--to VERSION` (default: the newest release), `--wp VERSION` (default latest), `--php VERSION` (default 8.3), `--keep-log FILE`. Read the releases with `gh release list` / `gh release download` on the repository in `GitHub Plugin URI`, so a private repository works too.
4. Checks, each printed as `ok` or `FAIL`, exit 1 on any failure:
   - Install `{slug}-FROM.zip` from the release (downloaded with `gh release download` and mounted read-only, as `smoke-test.sh` mounts `/zips`) and activate it; the version is FROM.
   - Fresh check through WP-CLI: `delete_site_transient('update_plugins'); wp_update_plugins();`. The `update_plugins` transient's `response['{slug}/{slug}.php']` has `new_version` TO and a `package` ending in `/{slug}-TO.zip` on GitHub.
   - Log in as the admin with curl (cookie jar) and load `wp-admin/update-core.php?force-check=1` (the **Check again** link): it lists `{Name}` and TO. `wp-admin/plugins.php` shows "There is a new version of {Name} available".
   - `wp plugin update {slug}`: the version is TO, the plugin is still active, no further update is offered, and `wp-admin/options-general.php?page={slug}` answers 200.
   - `wp-content/debug.log` is empty.
5. Private repositories: sites read releases without signing in, so the update check of a private repository needs a token (`RELEASING.md`, below step 4). When the environment has `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, set it in the test site's `wp-config.php` with `wp config set` (the shared updater reads that constant). Never print it, never write it to a file outside the throwaway volume, and never take it as a command-line argument.
6. Docs: `RELEASING.md` step 4 runs `scripts/update-test.sh` after `gh release create` (and keeps the hand check as the fallback), and the script table at the top of `RELEASING.md` lists it. Add a `changelog.txt` line under Unreleased (`README.md` and `readme.txt` get theirs at the next release).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck on the new script; every function has an explicit `return`, arguments read with `local name="$1"`).
- `scripts/update-test.sh --from 1.0.6 --to 1.0.7` passes on this repository's releases. With no options it picks the newest two releases and passes.
- `scripts/update-test.sh --to 9.9.9` fails with a clear message (no such release) and leaves no Docker containers, volumes or networks (`docker ps -a`, `docker volume ls`, `docker network ls`).
- A throwaway clone renamed with `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`: `scripts/update-test.sh --help` shows the new names, and `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` in the starter itself lists the new file as core.

title: fix: large changelog.txt can fail preflight checks (SIGPIPE with grep -q under pipefail)
body:
## What

Script checks that pipe a large variable into `grep -q` can report a false result. Use a here-string (`grep -q … <<<"$text"`) instead of `printf '%s\n' "$text" | grep -q …`.

## Why

The scripts run with `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits at its first match; when the text is larger than the pipe buffer (64 KB on macOS and Linux), `printf` is still writing and gets SIGPIPE. Its status 141 then fails the whole pipeline even though grep matched.

Seen in a plugin made from the starter: its `changelog.txt` is 67 KB, and `scripts/preflight-release.sh` alternated between `ok changelog.txt changelog has 0.12.7` and `warn changelog.txt changelog has no '= 0.12.7 =' entry` on the same commit. The entry is on line 13.

## How

Replace every `printf '%s\n' "$var" | grep -…q …` with `grep -…q … <<<"$var"`. Current places:

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: lines ~172 (Update URI), 198 and 203 (`check_changelog`), 268 (upgrade notice), 375 (zip file list), 518 and 525 (AGENTS.md).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` ~230 (debug log canary).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh` ~124 (Plugin Check report).

Small inputs are safe today, but all the places change together so the pattern does not come back.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck).
- With a `changelog.txt` over 64 KB that has the current version's entry near the top, `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` reports `ok changelog.txt changelog has <version>` on every run (for example 10 runs in a row).
- `rg -n "printf '%s\\\\n' \"\\$\\w+\" \\| grep -\\w*q" scripts` finds nothing.

title: fix: update-test.sh fails the update check with a token (API asset address)
body:
## What

`scripts/update-test.sh` reports `FAIL no offer of X.Y.Z from {slug}-X.Y.Z.zip (check that WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN can read {owner}/{repo})` whenever `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, even though the update is offered and installs.

## Evidence

Run on a private plugin made from the starter, with a token that can read it:

```text
Update check (WP-CLI):
  offer: X.Y.Z https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/assets/{id}
  FAIL no offer of X.Y.Z from {slug}-X.Y.Z.zip (check that WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN can read {owner}/{repo})
...
  ok   Updates screen lists {Name}: Update to X.Y.Z
  ok   version after the update: X.Y.Z
  ok   status after the update: active
```

With a token, the shared updater (`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`, `pick_asset()`) picks the asset named exactly `{folder}-{version}.zip` and offers its API address (`https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/assets/{id}`). Private repositories need that address, and the name is checked before it is chosen. `check_offer()` in `scripts/update-test.sh` accepts only a package address ending in `/{slug}-X.Y.Z.zip`, which is right without a token.

## How

`scripts/update-test.sh` → `check_offer()`: with a token, also accept `X.Y.Z https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/releases/assets/{digits}`. The test already checks the release has exactly one asset, `{slug}-X.Y.Z.zip`, so this ID can only be that asset. Without a token, keep requiring the public `/{slug}-X.Y.Z.zip` address.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (ShellCheck).
- `scripts/update-test.sh` on a public plugin without a token: unchanged `ok offers X.Y.Z from the release asset`.
- On a private plugin with `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN`: `ok` instead of `FAIL` at the WP-CLI check.

title: Add an OpenSSF Scorecard workflow (core file) for public plugins
body:
## What

Add an OpenSSF Scorecard workflow as a core file, so every plugin made from the starter gets it at public launch. `DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch: full sweep, step 1, already lists "OpenSSF Scorecard", but no workflow provides it. Found while running the sweep in SEO Pro Stack (wpallstars/seoprostack), which went public on 2026-10-04. CodeQL, Dependabot, secret scanning, push protection and the `main` ruleset were set up there through the API, but Scorecard needs a workflow file.

## How

- New `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`, modelled on `.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml` for structure and comments:
  - Triggers: `push` to the default branch, a weekly `schedule`, `branch_protection_rule`, and `workflow_dispatch`.
  - Top-level `permissions: read-all`. The job gets `security-events: write` (SARIF upload) and `id-token: write` (publish_results).
  - Steps: `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false`; `ossf/scorecard-action` with `results_file: results.sarif`, `results_format: sarif`, `publish_results: true`; then `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`.
  - Pin every action to a commit SHA with the version in a comment (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → Dependencies). Find the SHAs with `gh api repos/ossf/scorecard-action/releases/latest` and the matching tag ref; don't guess them.
  - Skip on private repositories (`if: github.event.repository.private == false`): Scorecard publishing needs a public repository, and private ones use paid minutes (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → While private).
- Add the workflow to `scripts/core-files.txt` and mention it in `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Checks, in the same style as SonarCloud and Starter sync.
- Optionally add the Scorecard badge to the README badges block for public plugins (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure).

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh workflows` (actionlint) passes.
- In a public plugin, after syncing core files: Actions → Scorecard → Run workflow succeeds, and the Security → Code scanning tab shows Scorecard results.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` in SEO Pro Stack lists the new file until it is synced.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`
- EDIT: `scripts/core-files.txt`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

title: fix: PHPStan level-7 findings in core files (GitHub updater, Read Me and admin managers)
body:
## What

Fix the PHPStan level-7 findings in the starter's core files, so plugins made from the starter can raise their level without per-plugin ignores for shared code. Found while working through the level-7 findings in a plugin made from the starter (wpallstars/seoprostack#395). That plugin can't fix them locally: `STANDARDS.md` says core files change in the starter first.

## Findings (file:line in the starter)

Real edge cases:

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:420` and `:934`: `(string) wp_remote_retrieve_header($response, 'location')`. The header is `string|array` (more than one `Location` header), and an array cast gives `"Array"` plus a warning. Take the last value: `is_array($h) ? (string) end($h) : (string) $h`.
- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:809` and `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php:50`: `foreach (preg_split('/\r\n|\r|\n/', ...) as $line)`. `preg_split()` returns `false` on a PCRE error; use `?: array()`.
- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:185-188, 202`: `filemtime()` is `int|false` and goes in as the style/script version, which WordPress types as `string|bool|null`. Use `(string) filemtime(...)` with a fallback to the version constant when it is `false`.

- `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:570` (`sanitize_lines()`) and `:609` (`parse_domains()`): `preg_split()` results go to `array_map()` / `foreach` unchecked; `false` on a PCRE error. Use `?: array()`.

Type-only (no runtime change):

- `class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:713, 716`: `$transient->response` / `->no_update` on `object`; type `@param \stdClass $transient`.
- `class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:169`: `plugins()` returns `non-empty-array`, not the documented shape; build each entry with all keys so the `array{repo, asset_only, github_only, version, name}` return holds.
- `class-admin-manager.php:202`: `$deps` from `apply_filters` is `array<string>`; filter out empty handles (`array_filter`) so it is `array<non-empty-string>`.

### Files Scope

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`
- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`
- `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`

## How to reproduce

From a plugin made from the starter, with its `phpstan.neon.dist`:

```
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --level=7 --memory-limit=4G --no-progress
```

then read the findings in `includes/github-updater/`, `admin/includes/` and the settings store. Ignore the `missingType.*` identifiers (noise tracked separately).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes at the current level.
- Level-7 run shows no findings in `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`, `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`, `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php` and `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php` (apart from the `rest_sanitize_boolean()` template-type note at `:447`, a stub limitation).
- Updates from GitHub still finds a release: on a test site with the starter active, **Dashboard → Updates → Check again** lists the newer GitHub release (or `wp plugin list --update=available` shows it), and the Read Me tab still renders.
- Bump the starter version and changelog as `RELEASING.md` says, so plugins can sync the core files.

title: Signed releases: build, attest and publish from a core release workflow
body:
## What

Build, sign and publish GitHub releases from a core workflow, so every release asset has Sigstore build provenance. OpenSSF Scorecard (added in 1.0.10) scores the starter 0 on **Signed-Releases**: releases are built and uploaded from a laptop, with no signature or provenance asset.

## How

- New core workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered by pushing a plain version tag (`vX.Y.Z`):
  - Checks the tag is on `main`, runs `scripts/preflight-release.sh --ref vX.Y.Z --offline --no-docker`, and builds with `scripts/build-release.sh --ref vX.Y.Z`.
  - `actions/attest-build-provenance` attests `{slug}-X.Y.Z.zip` (public repositories only: attestations on private ones need GitHub Enterprise Cloud).
  - Creates the release with the zip and the Sigstore bundle as `provenance-{slug}-X.Y.Z.sigstore.json`. Scorecard counts the `.sigstore.json` suffix. The name must not start with `{slug}`: Git Updater installs the first asset whose name starts with the slug. Release notes come from the version's section in `README.md`.
- `scripts/update-test.sh`: accept that one extra asset; still fail on any other.
- `RELEASING.md` step 3: tag and push; the workflow publishes. Local `gh release create` stays as the fallback. Verify with `gh attestation verify`.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh workflows shell` passes.
- Release 1.0.11 through the workflow: the release has the zip and the bundle, `gh attestation verify dist/{slug}-1.0.11.zip --repo {owner}/{repo}` passes, and `scripts/update-test.sh` passes.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- EDIT: `scripts/update-test.sh`, `RELEASING.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md`, changelogs

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: fix: preflight-release.sh exits 141 (SIGPIPE) on a README.md over 64 KB
body:
## What

`scripts/preflight-release.sh` stops with exit 141 (SIGPIPE) and no message right after "Versions and headers" when `README.md` is larger than the pipe buffer (64 KB on macOS and Linux).

`check_readme_version()` (added in 1.0.13, #339) runs:

```bash
line="$(git show "$sha:README.md" | sed -nE '/^Version:/{s/^Version:[[:space:]]*//p;q;}')"
```

`sed` quits at the first `Version:` line. With a long README, `git show` is still writing, gets SIGPIPE, and under `set -o pipefail` the assignment fails, so `set -e` ends the script. The starter's own README is small enough that `git show` finishes first, so the starter never sees it. SEO Pro Stack's README (about 200 KB) fails every time after syncing core from `main` (wpallstars/seoprostack#409).

## How

In `scripts/preflight-release.sh` → `check_readme_version()`, read the whole stream and keep the first match in Bash, so nothing closes the pipe early:

```bash
line="$(git show "$sha:README.md" | sed -nE 's/^Version:[[:space:]]*//p')"
line="${line%%$'\n'*}"
```

Add a Fixed line to the Unreleased changelog (`README.md`, `changelog.txt`; `readme.txt` only if it has room — it is a developer change, so a `Developers:` line).

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` (shell) passes.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` in the starter: unchanged output, `README.md Version: matches`.
- In a SEO Pro Stack worktree after `scripts/sync-core.sh --ref origin/main`: preflight runs to the end and prints `README.md Version: matches`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/preflight-release.sh`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`

title: feat: release channels (GitHub stable beta, WordPress.org after 90 days unless security) and no affiliate links in the WordPress.org build
body:
## What

Owner's decisions (2026-10-04, from wpallstars/seoprostack's WordPress.org guideline review):

1. **Release channels.** GitHub releases are the **stable beta** channel. A version goes to WordPress.org 90 days after its GitHub release, unless it is a security release, which goes to WordPress.org straight away. Applies to every plugin made from the starter.
2. **No affiliate links in the WordPress.org build.** WordPress.org's guideline 11 does not permit tracking referrals in the dashboard, and guideline 12 requires affiliate links to point straight at the service, not through a redirect. GitHub builds keep their referral links; the WordPress.org build swaps each one for the plain address.

## How

- `STANDARDS.md` → Releases and `RELEASING.md` → WordPress.org: the two channels, the 90-day wait, the security exception, and that the WordPress.org release is built from the GitHub tag of the version.
- New optional `.wporg-links` file (the plugin's own, read from Git like `.distignore-wporg`; kept out of both zips, `export-ignore`): one `from-URL<TAB>to-URL` pair per line. `scripts/build-release.sh` replaces each `from` (and its `&` / `&` forms) with `to` in the WordPress.org tree's text files.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: errors when a listed `from` URL is still in the WordPress.org build; warns about URLs with referral-style query parameters (`ref`, `aff`, `irpid`, `refcode`, `referralcode`, `referral_code`, `via`...) left there.
- `README.md` → Updates and releases (template text) and `DEVELOPMENT.md` wording where they mention early updates.

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` on the starter (no `.wporg-links`: notes it, no errors). Then in wpallstars/seoprostack with its `.wporg-links`: preflight shows the WordPress.org build without any listed affiliate URL, and the GitHub build unchanged.

title: STANDARDS.md: defaults reach new installs only, %i for identifiers, removable notice arguments, NOSONAR reasons; release 1.0.17
body:
## What

Four rules SEO Pro Stack learned that apply to every plugin made from the starter, added to `STANDARDS.md`, then release 1.0.16.

1. **A changed default reaches new installs only.** `{Prefix}_Settings::maybe_migrate()` stores `sanitize_all()`, which starts from `all()` (defaults included), so the first migration stores every setting. A later change to a default never reaches existing sites; a new setting's default reaches every site. Goes next to "Features are off by default" (Structure).
2. **Table and column names through `$wpdb->prepare()` with `%i`** (WordPress 6.2+, the minimum), never interpolated; core tables through `$wpdb->posts` and the like. Plugin Check reports `PluginCheck.Security.DirectDB.UnescapedDBParameter` otherwise (SEO Pro Stack had 3 before its WordPress.org submission). Code rules.
3. **One-off result notices register their query arguments with `removable_query_args`**, so a reload does not show the notice again. Code rules.
4. **An inline `NOSONAR` needs the reason on that line**, as `phpcs:ignore` already does; `md5()` used as a fingerprint or cache key (not security) is the usual case. Code rules.

## Files

- `STANDARDS.md` (Structure, Code rules)
- Release 1.0.16: `wp-plugin-starter-template.php` (`Version:`, `WPSTARTER_VERSION`), `readme.txt` (Stable tag, changelog), `README.md` (Version line, changelog), `changelog.txt`.

The aidevops push gate (`complexity-regression-helper.sh`, file-size metric) blocks a push that takes a non-README Markdown file past 500 lines. `STANDARDS.md` is a core file that every plugin copies word for word, so each plugin's starter sync fails at push. SEO Pro Stack's sync (wpallstars/seoprostack#422) stopped on exactly this: its copy is 468 lines, and the starter's is 508.

## How

- `STANDARDS.md`: tighten wording and merge repeated points (the same rule stated in two places, long examples) until it is about 480 lines, leaving room for later rules. Keep every rule and every file, script and setting name.
- Bump the version and changelog for a patch release (`RELEASING.md` → GitHub release).

## Verify

- `wc -l STANDARDS.md` under 500 (aim ~480).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` has 0 errors; `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- Then in SEO Pro Stack: `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` lists `STANDARDS.md` and the push gate passes.

title: docs: STANDARDS.md allows indexes on other tables, never duplicate ones
body:
## What

`STANDARDS.md` → Performance: replace "Never add indexes to WordPress's own tables" with "never add an index that duplicates one a table already has". Other plugins may already have added the same index. Then release the starter.

## Why

Owner's decision (wpallstars/seoprostack#65, "Database index advisor"). An opt-in index on a core table can be worth adding. The real harm is a second copy of an index that another plugin, or the site's host, already added: it slows every write and saves no reads.

## How

- `STANDARDS.md` → Performance, the "Index the plugin's own tables" bullet. Check a table's existing keys (`SHOW INDEX`) before adding one, and skip it when a key with the same leading columns exists. An index on a table the plugin does not own is opt-in and removed on uninstall.
- Search the starter's other docs for the old rule and update them to match.
- Patch release (version, `README.md`/`changelog.txt`/`readme.txt` changelog).

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` has 0 errors; `wc -l STANDARDS.md` is under 500.
- In SEO Pro Stack, `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` lists `STANDARDS.md` until it is synced.

title: quality: settings save lock takeover race and sanitizer guards
body:
Parent: #362

## What

Fix the settings save lock's takeover race, and harden the settings sanitizers. Found in the second audit (CodeRabbit full review and Codacy on `2a2037c`, checked against the code).

## Findings

- **Medium**, `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:272-298` (`lock()`, `unlock()`). Taking over a stale lock is racy. Requests A and B both read the same stale timestamp. A runs `unlock()` and inserts a fresh lock. B then runs `unlock()`, which deletes A's fresh lock, and inserts its own, so both hold the lock and one save overwrites the other. `unlock()` also deletes whatever row is there, so a request whose lock was taken over deletes the new owner's lock when it finishes.
  Fix: store a unique value per request (for example `time() . ':' . wp_generate_uuid4()`) and parse the time from it for the `LOCK_TIMEOUT` test. Take over with `DELETE ... WHERE option_name = %s AND option_value = %s` using the stale value just read, then retry the `INSERT IGNORE`. `unlock()` deletes only the row holding this request's own value. Keep `INSERT IGNORE` as the lock (see the docblock for why `add_option()` is not used).
- **Low**, `:249-251` (`set()`). It writes back `self::all()`, and `all()` keeps only keys in `schema()` at that moment (`:210`). A stored value whose setting is not registered on this request (a feature registered conditionally, an add-on switched off) is deleted by the next save of any other setting. Fix: under the lock, read the raw stored array, set the one sanitized key, and write that back.
- **Low**, `:593` and the other sanitizers that cast `(string) $value`. `ajax_save` passes arrays through, so posting `value[]=x` for a text setting gives an "Array to string conversion" notice. Fix: for scalar types, treat a non-scalar value as invalid (return the default, as other invalid values do).
- **Low**, `:561-562` (URL sanitizer, relative paths). `/\evil.com` passes, and browsers read `/\` as `//`. No redirect uses these values yet, so it is latent. Fix: reject relative values containing `\`.
- **Low**, `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js:144-181` (`Settings.save`). `run` refers to `done` and `failed` before they are defined (Codacy `no-use-before-define`, 4 items). It works because `run` is only called later through `this.queue.then`. Fix: define `done` and `failed` before `run`, with no change in behaviour.

## Constraints

Both are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`); plugins take the fix with `scripts/sync-core.sh`. The AJAX contract (`wpstarter_save_setting`, the response's `value`/`reload`/`message`) stays the same.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (PHPCS, PHPStan level 7, JS); CI smoke tests and Plugin Check pass.
- On a local site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), quick saves of two settings from two tabs both persist; a lock row older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT` is taken over, and the save succeeds.
- Codacy on the PR shows no `no-use-before-define` in `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`.

## Files Scope

- `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`
- `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`

title: quality: GitHub updater repository case, renamed repositories, token docs
body:
Parent: #362

## What

Small fixes to the shared GitHub updater, found in the second audit (CodeRabbit full review on `2a2037c`, checked against the code).

## Findings (`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`)

- **Low**, `:585`. `strpos($public, self::GITHUB . $repo . ...)` is case-sensitive, and `$repo` comes from the plugin's `GitHub Plugin URI` header, while GitHub returns the repository's canonical case. A header written in another case finds no release asset, so the updater falls back to the source zipball (unless `Release Asset: true` is set). Fix: compare without regard to case (`stripos`, or lower-case both).
- **Low**, `:448`. A renamed repository answers with a 301 to a different path. The regex does not match, and the result is silently "no release". Fix: when the redirect points to another repository, return a `WP_Error` naming the new `owner/repo` so the plugin's header can be corrected. Do not follow the redirect: requests never follow redirects on purpose.
- **Low**, docblock `:21-30` and `:407-409`. With any token set, every repository is read through the API, public ones too. The docblock says public repositories use github.com pages. Document the token case.

Declined: the worst case of three serial 10-second requests per plugin (`:433-487`) runs only when the update transient is refreshed (12-hourly, as for WordPress.org plugins).

## Constraints

Only the newest copy of this class runs on a site (other wpallstars plugins ship it too). Raise the version in `includes/github-updater/load.php:34` (now `1.1.0`) with any change to the class. Keep request URLs, redirect handling, private-download handling and version comparison otherwise identical; do not rename the class or public methods.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes; CI smoke tests and Plugin Check pass.
- An update check against a real GitHub release still finds the update on a local site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), and still finds it with the header's `owner/repo` in a different case.

## Files Scope

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `includes/github-updater/load.php`

title: quality: test scripts fail when they cannot check, clean up every container, exact update offer
body:
Parent: #362

## What

Make the test scripts fail when they cannot check, clean up every container, and check the exact update offer. Found in the second audit (CodeRabbit full review and a script review on `2a2037c`, checked against the code).

## Findings

- **Medium**, `scripts/smoke-test.sh:224-227` (`check_uninstall`). `left="$(wp_cli option list ... 2>/dev/null || true)"`: if WP-CLI fails (for example its container does not start), `left` is empty and the check reports nothing left. The cron check is the same. Fix: capture WP-CLI's output and status separately and `fail` when it fails; only then filter with `grep`, treating no match as "nothing left".
- **Low**, `scripts/smoke-test.sh:255-257` (`check_queries`). `report="$(wp_cli eval ...)" || true` then greps for `queries: ok`. Require a zero exit status as well as the verdict.
- **Medium**, `scripts/smoke-test.sh:78-82` and `scripts/update-test.sh:94-98` (`cleanup`). They remove the web and db containers, then the volume and network, once. A WP-CLI container still stopping (after Ctrl-C) keeps the volume and network in use, so removal fails silently and they are left. Fix: use the pattern in `scripts/plugin-check.sh:53-68` (remove containers using the volume, then retry the volume and network removal up to three times, with a message if it still fails).
- **Medium**, `scripts/update-test.sh:273` (`check_offer`). `"$TO https://"*"/$SLUG-$TO.zip"*` accepts any host, path prefix and suffix. Fix: compare with the exact `https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/v$TO/$SLUG-$TO.zip` (keep the token branch on the next line as it is).
- **Low**, `scripts/update-test.sh:154, 163-164`. A failing `gh release view` exits under `set -e` with no message; add a `die` naming the release. The `--jq` filter is built by joining in `$SLUG`; pass values with `--jq` and `env.` or `--arg`-style input instead.
- **Low**, `scripts/update-test.sh:244`. `curl -w '%{http_code}' ... || printf '000'` gives `000000` on failure (still fails, but the message is wrong). Follow `scripts/preflight-release.sh:157`.
- **Low**, `scripts/update-test.sh:181-182`. `gh attestation verify --source-ref` needs a recent `gh`; when verification fails, say which `gh` version is needed so an old `gh` is not mistaken for a bad build.
- **Low**, `scripts/update-test.sh:290`. Add `|| true` to `wp transient delete` (it exits non-zero if the transient is missing).
- **Low**, `scripts/smoke-queries.php:372-377`. With a wrong `WPALLSTARS_SMOKE_PLUGIN`, no query is the plugin's (`$mine = 0`) and the report still says `queries: ok`; the canary proves EXPLAIN works, not attribution. Fix: print a note when `$mine` is 0 (the starter itself may make none, so do not fail).
- **Low**, `scripts/smoke-queries.php:152-160`. `json_encode` returns `false` on invalid UTF-8 and the log line is dropped silently. Use `JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE` and check `file_put_contents`.
- **Low**, `scripts/smoke-queries.php:243`. `$scans[$step['type']]` can use `null` as an array key (deprecated in PHP 8.5). Cast with `(string)`.
- **Low**, `scripts/plugin-check.sh:136-201`. When Plugin Check exits non-zero after reporting only the expected updater errors, subtracting them leaves 0 and the run passes, even if it stopped part way (for example a PHP fatal error). Fix: fail when the report contains `Fatal error` or `Allowed memory size`, whatever the counts.

Declined, with reasons recorded in #362: signal traps (bash 3.2 and 5.3 both run the EXIT trap on SIGTERM and SIGINT), an EXPLAIN that fails (already printed as "not checked"), and queries changed through hooks such as `pre_get_posts` (outside what stack attribution measures).

## Constraints

Core files: plugins take the fix with `scripts/sync-core.sh`. Must run on macOS bash 3.2 with BSD tools and on Ubuntu CI. ShellCheck stays clean.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes; CI smoke tests (both matrices) and Plugin Check pass.
- `scripts/update-test.sh` passes for the latest release; stopping it with Ctrl-C during the update leaves no `docker ps -a`, `docker volume ls` or `docker network ls` entries for its name.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passes; with Docker stopped part way it fails rather than passing.

## Files Scope

- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- `scripts/update-test.sh`
- `scripts/smoke-queries.php`
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
